- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.27) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% and add a slight downward slope after peak.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.77) and price is trending up, model frequently overestimates future values; cap forecast at 1.2x recent 10-day moving average to avoid overbought bias.
- When sentiment swings from negative to positive (e.g., 0.00 → 0.77), model often lags; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead to align with sentiment momentum.
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates mean-reversion zones; add 0.5–1.0% buffer above recent 10-day average to account for lagged correction.
- If sentiment is negative and price is falling, model often forecasts a steeper decline; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% to avoid panic-driven underestimation.
